messages.subject: Re: changing sequence of default colors
parts:
If your colors are based on factor variables, you can always rearrange
them (?levels) into the 'correct' order. In addition, I'd suggest
reading ?scale_colour_brewer and associated pages. These give lots of
examples of using a particular palette.

Ben

messages.author: ea0dc7d20f577516
messages.subject: Re: changing sequence of default colors
parts:
Hi SP

A factor can have many levels even if they don't appear in a given data frame.  So as you as your factor in each data.frame has all four levels defined and they are in the same order, they will always be coloured similarly.

That's my understanding at least.

So if you have two levels, Apple and Orange, but other levels are possible (in other datasets) like Banana and Pear, then you can define:

factor(c("Apple", "Apple", "Orange"), levels = c("Apple", "Orange", "Banana", "Pear"))

The unused levels will still be "assigned" colours (according to the order they in which they appear in your levels definition).

Regards,
Benjamin
